Summary: A presence. The image would be part of a sequence that was taken in San José de Catemu, V region, around 10:41 on November 10, 2018.

User description:

They see two ships in a sequence of photographs they took.

They were analyzed with ELA (Error Level Analysis) and CMF (Copy and Motion Forgery) so it was determined they were not digitally altered.

The metadata indicated that the photos were taken with a Motorola G4 cellphone at the time noted in the report. With this information, both meteorology and air traffic could be studied.

The consistency of the meteorological conditions at the reported time with those present in the images provided for analysis was verified. According to the collected data, very good conditions were presented.

Investigation: visibility with winds whose intensity increased gradually, varying from Southeast to Northeast and being particularly unstable at the time of the photographic captures. The detail of the records directly related to the case is as follows:

Figure 1 shows the location from which the reported sighting was made, which corresponds to a valley surrounded by hills, and is also located in the middle of very busy air routes to the north of the Santiago valley (Figure 2).

Figure 1. General location.

The air traffic associated with the reported period was reviewed, finding that, without following the usual pattern of aircraft circulating over the air routes,

The approach to Comodoro Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCEL) of flight LA 121, originating from Andrés Sabella Aerodrome in Antofagasta (SCFA), was verified. It involved an Airbus 321-211, registration CC-BEH, flying at approximately 13,175 feet and 280 knots on a 215° heading. (Figure 2)

On November 20, 2018, technical advice was requested from the Wildlife Ecology Laboratory (LEVS) of the University of Chile. Additionally,

An independent peritage was requested from the National Museum of Natural History, MNHN (03 May 2019).
